name: @w6w-apps/postgres
description: Run SQL directly against a PostgreSQL database over its own wire protocol.

w6w.longDescription:
PostgreSQL is a raw database, not an HTTP API — there is no vendor REST surface to call, so this app speaks the Postgres wire protocol (v3.0) directly: it authenticates with SCRAM-SHA-256, the mechanism every current PostgreSQL install negotiates by default, and sends a workflow's SQL to the server exactly as written.

The connect form collects host, port, database, TLS mode, and a username/password pair once; the host resolves and pre-checks that target before ever dialing it, and the SCRAM exchange runs as an iterative, network-less hook so the password itself never leaves the sandbox that holds it. `query` then runs over the resulting authenticated socket and returns whatever rows come back.

There is deliberately no parameter-binding syntax (`$1`, a `params` array) in this version — the caller's SQL is sent verbatim as a Simple Query, so building a statement safely is the caller's job, the same way it would be with `psql` or any other client that has not yet added prepared statements.
